gate.rationale: The course entry, immediate predecessor, sole hard prerequisite, notation ledger, research brief, pedagogy rubric, and gold lesson agree on one teachable move: turn the finite-record DTFT samples already computed in the predecessor into a fully declared DFT interface, then hand the unchanged coefficients to the FFT lesson. The proposed six-section argument covers every course-entry key idea and the required demo without importing later window-design material.

spine_alignment.course_governing_question: How can a finite stream of samples support a trustworthy claim about a physical signal and a reliable implemented system?
spine_alignment.spine_step: The DFT supplies finite coordinates and the FFT computes them efficiently; a DTMF receiver turns coefficients into a constrained decision.
inherits: DTFT and Frequency Response established that a finite record defines a continuous, 2pi-periodic DTFT and that zero padding merely samples that same curve more densely.
DTFT and Frequency Response established real-sequence conjugacy and the distinction between DTFT parentheses and finite DFT brackets.
Sampling, Aliasing, and Reconstruction established the map from hertz to periodic radians/sample and ended with the exact eight correlations for x[n]=cos(2pi(2/8)n).
spine_alignment.opens: A finite record needs a declared coordinate system: transform sign, scale, bin order, physical-frequency map, real-spectrum reporting rule, and boundary convention.
spine_alignment.contributes: Compute and interpret an N-point DFT under one explicit interface, including conjugate symmetry, normalization, and circular convolution.
spine_alignment.handoff_boundary: This lesson fixes what the coefficients mean and what exact result is required; the FFT lesson changes only how those same coefficients are computed and stored efficiently.

opening_verbatim_check.required: The DFT samples one period of a finite record’s spectrum and therefore inherits both periodic indexing and implementation conventions.
opening_verbatim_check.planned_first_sentence: The DFT samples one period of a finite record’s spectrum and therefore inherits both periodic indexing and implementation conventions.
throughline_after_opening: Sampling, Aliasing, and Reconstruction ended by computing eight harmonic correlations for one finite record; DTFT and Frequency Response explains why those eight values lie on one continuous, periodic frequency function.
This lesson names that finite coordinate system and asks what must be declared before its numbers can support an engineering claim.

The route fixes the transform pair, maps bins to signed frequency, exploits but does not overclaim real-input symmetry, reconciles scale conventions, distinguishes circular from linear convolution, and leaves the same coefficients ready for FFT factorization.

retrieval_gate.placement: Immediately after the opening throughline and before the first new definition.

prompts.prompt: For a finite sequence x[n] that is zero outside 0 <= n < N, write its DTFT with the course analysis sign and state its frequency periodicity.
prompts.success_criterion: Writes X(e^{j omega})=sum_n x[n]e^{-j omega n} and states 2pi periodicity.

prompts.prompt: For real x[n], state the conjugacy relation between X(e^{j omega}) and X(e^{-j omega}); then say what must be true at the self-conjugate frequencies 0 and pi when the value is nonzero.
prompts.success_criterion: States X(e^{-j omega})=X*(e^{j omega}) and that the values at 0 and pi are real, with phase undefined at a zero.

prompts.prompt: A three-sample record is zero-padded before evaluating more frequency points. What changed in the stored sequence and what did not change about its continuous DTFT?
prompts.success_criterion: Distinguishes appended zeros and a denser evaluation grid from added observation or a changed finite-record DTFT.

prompts.prompt: Without recomputing all eight sums, recall the nonzero correlations for x[n]=cos(2pi(2/8)n), n=0,...,7, and explain why they occur as a pair.
prompts.success_criterion: Recalls X[2]=X[6]=4 with all other bins zero and attributes the pair to the conjugate positive- and negative-frequency components of a real cosine.

retrieval_gate.pass_rule: Proceed when R1 and R2 are correct and at least one of R3 or R4 is correct. Otherwise route the learner back to DTFT and Frequency Response; a miss only on R4 can be repaired by reopening the predecessor's final exercise.

argument_skeleton.heading: Eight correlations become one declared transform
argument_skeleton.running_question: What exactly were the eight numbers computed at the end of the previous lesson?
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Reuse x[n]=cos(2pi(2/8)n) and [0,0,4,0,0,0,4,0] without repeating eight full correlations.
argument_skeleton.claim: For a record supported on 0 <= n < N, the N-point DFT is the record's DTFT sampled at omega_k=2pi k/N; roots-of-unity orthogonality supplies the inverse.
required_apparatus: Definition of the forward and inverse N-point DFT under the house convention
Short roots-of-unity orthogonality derivation of inversion
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: The coefficients are coordinates against a declared finite basis, not a detector list containing only sinusoids physically present in the record.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: The sum now produces N valid coefficients, but a coefficient index still has neither a hertz value nor a unique left-to-right plotting position.

argument_skeleton.heading: A bin acquires hertz only from N and the sample rate
argument_skeleton.running_question: What frequency does index k denote?
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Label the N=8 record at f_s=8 kHz in raw unshifted order, signed wrapped order, and an explicitly shifted display.
argument_skeleton.claim: omega_k=2pi k/N and f_k=k f_s/N only after N and f_s are declared; bins above the positive-frequency range are wrapped negative frequencies, with an explicit Nyquist tie for even N.
required_apparatus: Raw-index, signed-frequency, and fftshift mapping table
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: High array indices are not automatically high positive frequencies; in unshifted storage they often represent negative-frequency directions.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: Once the signed locations are visible, the paired values in a real record demand an exact symmetry rule rather than a plotting shortcut.

argument_skeleton.heading: Real records halve storage, not the transform
argument_skeleton.running_question: Which coefficients are determined by others, and which must not be doubled?
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Apply X[N-k]=X*[k] to the N=8 cosine, then isolate DC and the even-N Nyquist bin as self-conjugate real values.
argument_skeleton.claim: Real input gives conjugate-symmetric DFT coefficients; a one-sided amplitude report may double paired interior magnitudes, but DC and an even-N Nyquist bin remain singletons, and phase-sensitive inversion retains the complex pair or an equivalent packed representation.
required_apparatus: Conjugate-symmetry derivation from the DFT definition
Full-spectrum, one-sided amplitude, and packed-real layout ledger
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: Redundancy permits compressed storage or one-sided reporting, but it does not license doubling every displayed bin or discarding the phase needed for reconstruction.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: Symmetry fixes relationships among bins, but it does not fix their numerical scale; two correct implementations can still disagree by N or sqrt(N).

argument_skeleton.heading: Scaling is an interface contract
argument_skeleton.running_question: Why can correct libraries report different coefficient magnitudes for the same record?
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: For N=8 and x[n]=(-1)^n, compare the house result X[4]=8 with a unitary result of magnitude sqrt(8), then recover the same samples under the paired inverse convention.
argument_skeleton.claim: Analysis and synthesis factors must multiply to 1/N; the course uses an unscaled forward transform and a 1/N inverse, and Parseval's identity carries the corresponding 1/N energy factor.
required_apparatus: Compact normalization ledger translating house, unitary, and inverse-unscaled conventions
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: A factor-of-N amplitude discrepancy can be a convention translation rather than a numerical error, but only a declared forward/inverse pair makes that judgment possible.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: With sign, order, and scale fixed, pointwise multiplication has an exact time-domain meaning—and its boundary rule is the remaining surprise.

argument_skeleton.heading: DFT multiplication wraps the convolution
argument_skeleton.running_question: What time-domain operation does X[k]H[k] compute on a finite buffer?
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Use x=[1,2] and h=[1,-1]: the two-point circular result [-1,1] differs from the zero-extended linear result [1,1,-2], while length-three zero padding makes them agree.
argument_skeleton.claim: Pointwise multiplication of N-point DFTs produces convolution modulo N; it reproduces a finite linear convolution only when N is at least L_x+L_h-1 and both inputs are padded to that length.
required_apparatus: Short DFT multiplication derivation with indices reduced modulo N
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: The DTFT convolution theorem does not make an unpadded finite DFT buffer obey zero-extended linear convolution; the DFT has imposed periodic boundaries.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: Padding can prevent time-domain wrap, but padding used only to request more spectral samples solves a different problem and cannot lengthen the observation.

argument_skeleton.heading: More plotted bins do not add observation, and faster evaluation does not change the DFT
argument_skeleton.running_question: Which changes improve the view or the computation without changing the evidence or the coefficients?
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Use PaddingVsDataLab: zero padding drives a one-tone peak-location error below 0.1 original bins yet fails to create two phase-stable maxima for an unresolved two-tone record; a genuinely longer record can cross that resolution threshold.
argument_skeleton.claim: Zero padding samples the same finite-record DTFT more densely, whereas a longer record changes the observed data and its resolving power; FFT factorization will evaluate the already-declared DFT more efficiently without changing its coefficients.
required_apparatus: Required PaddingVsDataLab with the course-entry pass/fail rule
Same-data unpadded/padded versus genuinely longer-record comparison
Final synthesis ledger: index, units, sign, scale, symmetry, boundary
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: A smoother spectrum is not new resolution, and an FFT is not a different transform.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: The coefficient contract is complete; the next lesson may now change arithmetic count, factorization, storage order, and implementation layout without changing the mathematical output.

keeper_numbers.value: For N=8, x[n]=cos(2pi(2/8)n) gives X[2]=X[6]=4 and all other bins zero.
keeper_numbers.purpose: Carries the predecessor's exact forward exercise into the DFT definition, bin map, and real-input symmetry.

keeper_numbers.value: For N=8, x[n]=(-1)^n gives house-convention X[4]=8, while unitary scaling reports magnitude sqrt(8).
keeper_numbers.purpose: Pins down the self-conjugate Nyquist bin and makes normalization differences auditable.

keeper_numbers.value: For x=[1,2] and h=[1,-1], N=2 circular convolution is [-1,1]; length-3 linear convolution is [1,1,-2] and is recovered by padding to N=3.
keeper_numbers.purpose: Makes the periodic-boundary reversal visible in the smallest useful example.

items.prompt_contract: Compute the unscaled four-point DFT of x=[1,0,-1,0] at f_s=8 kHz; tabulate k, signed frequency, and complex X[k], verify conjugate symmetry, and invert with 1/N.
Handle N=1, constant input, alternating input, and even/odd N self-conjugate-bin cases without duplicating DC or Nyquist energy.
Refute 'DFT output is nonzero only at physically present sinusoids' with an off-bin finite cosine; identify the finite-record gate as the source of nonzero samples across the same continuous DTFT.
Derive Parseval's identity under the house DFT scaling and verify it on a short real sequence.

For a real 1 kHz cosine sampled at 8 kHz with N=8, choose a two-sided complex DFT for phase-sensitive reconstruction and a one-sided amplitude spectrum for amplitude reporting; produce both with the correct interior factor of two and verify reconstruction.
Split an eight-sample DFT sum into even and odd time indices, identify the repeated four-point sums and twiddle combination, and name the reuse formalized by FFT Factorization and Machine Layout.

required_fft_handoff.placement: Final paragraph of the final content section, before Exercises.
required_fft_handoff.draftable_text: At this point the DFT's coefficients, order, units, normalization, symmetry, and wrap rule are fixed. <Ref lesson="fft-factorization-and-layout">FFT Factorization and Machine Layout</Ref> next exploits repeated roots of unity to compute exactly these coefficients with fewer operations, while making storage ordering and scaling observable interface contracts.
must_preserve: An FFT computes the same DFT coefficients; it is not a different transform.
The next lesson owns arithmetic cost, factorization, in-place layout, permutations, and implementation scaling checks.
Do not preview a complete butterfly derivation in this lesson outside the single forward exercise.

nonblocking_risks.risk: The predecessor already writes the DFT formula and names the eight correlations as a DFT.
nonblocking_risks.control: Open by explicitly inheriting that result; add the inverse, declarations, symmetry, scaling, and boundary meaning instead of staging a false first encounter.

nonblocking_risks.risk: PaddingVsDataLab touches leakage and resolution, concepts owned by later lessons.
nonblocking_risks.control: Use it only to falsify the claim that a denser DFT grid adds observation; defer window metrics and estimators.

nonblocking_risks.risk: A broad survey of named FFT-library conventions could become software trivia or age quickly.
nonblocking_risks.control: Teach a compact algebraic translation ledger and verify any named library behavior only during drafting if it is retained.
